context: Checkpoint 2026-07-22 (13th). ROOT CAUSE FOUND for every failed LAN dialect from the phone: NOT ufw (operator disabled it; my detection wrongly read the service not ufw.conf ENABLED) but Trend Micro Deep Security (ds_agent) — a MANAGED CORPORATE endpoint agent (host serpro-*, corporate VPN) dropping inbound probes by policy, unfixable with the operator's sudo. Detection corrected and typed by fixability (5aaaf899): firewalls get scoped allow rules, endpoint agents get named + pointed at the P2P rail, no false sudo rule. This corporate host-lock makes the Pears/tunnel rail the ONLY viable cross-device path here, not a nice-to-have.
current_tasks: Commit 5aaaf899 — honest inbound-filter detection; 1629 tests green.
next_actions: The LAN rail is BLOCKED BY CORPORATE POLICY on this host — pivot to distribution + P2P. Distribution rung 2: bundle apps/refarm CLI to a single .mjs on the PC (verify no native deps in CLI graph), ship as GitHub Release asset, farm-hello fetches once. This gets refarm (not scripts) onto the phone regardless of the network wall.

P2P rail (Pears spec) rises to PRIMARY: it is LAN-independent, so ds_agent's inbound filter is irrelevant — outbound hyperswarm connections punch out. Start spec fatia 1 research (hyperswarm API, CGNAT/mobile hole-punch, bare-on-Android).

Cloudflare tunnel is the pragmatic bridge meanwhile: cloudflared makes an OUTBOUND connection from the host (ds_agent allows outbound), giving a stable https hostname the phone reaches from anywhere — no inbound hole needed. Strong candidate for the FIRST working cross-device demo.
